candidate_relations.reason: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated myositis is an incompatible autoimmune cause and is not supported by negative autoimmune serology.
Myocarditis is a documented organ manifestation of the systemic viral illness, not echovirus 11 itself.
Polymyositis names an idiopathic inflammatory myopathy rather than echovirus 11 infection.
Inflammatory myopathy with myocardial involvement describes the syndrome but omits echovirus 11.
Paraneoplastic myositis is not supported with CT showing no lymphoma relapse.
Sarcoid myositis is a different granulomatous myopathy.
Myositis associated with thymoma is not suggested by imaging.
Acute myelitis is a CNS manifestation on spinal MRI, not the viral diagnosis.
Systemic inflammatory disease is a nonspecific parent missing the echovirus etiology.
Mixed connective-tissue disease is not supported by negative autoimmune serology.
Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy is a different myositis subtype from enteroviral infection.
Ibrutinib-associated myositis was considered because of drug exposure but is an incompatible etiology relative to echovirus 11.
Ibrutinib-induced myositis likewise names a drug cause rather than echovirus 11.
Rhabdomyolysis is a complication of severe myositis causing AKI, not the infection itself.
Transverse myelitis describes the spinal lesion, a manifestation of the systemic infection.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate; echovirus 11 infection is not named
CSF/virus identification is not reported in the supplied excerpt despite myelitis/myocarditis
